verdicts.rationale: _load_terminal_page gates resume on winning_output.status == SUCCESS but never checks audit_passed. In agentic all-reject best-effort, att.output.audit_passed is set to att.accepted (False), yet the provider's status stays SUCCESS; _winning_page_output returns that best_output for scanned pages (no native text, no whole-doc), so the terminal sidecar freezes status=SUCCESS + audit_passed=False. On resume the ledger skips the page and restores judge-rejected text — silent corpus poisoning. The fix is a one-line gate: require audit_passed=True alongside SUCCESS, plus coverage for the SUCCESS+audit_passed=False sidecar shape.

verdicts.rationale: route_page, _TimeoutJudge.assess, and _escalate_table_page all use future.cancel() + shutdown(wait=False), which cannot stop an already-running call. agentic.py's comment calls the abandoned thread 'daemon', but tables/extract.py's own note states ThreadPoolExecutor workers are NOT daemon and keep the process alive while blocked. A permanently wedged provider/judge can therefore keep the CLI alive past its deadline. The fix (killable process boundary or daemon workers) is real but the process-boundary path is more than a trivial change, hence medium confidence on one-night fit.
